text.content:
Called the Dead Worlds, Mechanus is a Dyson Sphere filling its Crystal Sphere: a single colossal engine where planet-sized gears turn, pistons pump and everything glows in a sickly green light. Its builders and keepers are the Modrons, near-mindless immortals of living metal that wipe out any life they find. They are stirring from a long dormancy, and some scholars fear a coming March that would sterilize the whole Astral Sea. For now they are only partly awake, so the place is as deadly as a running engine rather than an active hunter.

Most structures are necrodermis, the living metal. Warp energy does not work here: spells fizzle, enchanted weapons go dull and magical wards drop, and the effect grows stronger the deeper one goes, until even minor magic fails. The interior holds oil seas, chimney and pipe thickets, and bolts of impossible green lightning. Intruders soon attract defense systems of overwhelming power, and the grinding machinery has never been charted; only small, nimble ships get far in, and few of those come back.

Only Modrons live in Mechanus. Meeting any sizeable group of them is hopeless even with divine help; the sensible response is to flee as quietly as possible, ideally alongside someone slower and expendable. Fighting achieves nothing, because destroyed Modrons return almost at once, and each moment of combat rouses still more of them to join the hunt.

Black Oil Sea: vast pools of oil that move as if alive, with unnatural waves and currents writhing like worms. The oil carries a disease that eats living flesh, and unproven tales claim it can turn ordinary machinery into necrodermis and Modron technology. The Pylon Forest: ranks of identical, motionless machines that bend magic around them like mirrors or lightning rods. Their purpose is unknown; some theorize their branches reach into the warp or a higher dimension and act as beacons for the Modrons' spell-free teleportation. The Afterlife: wryly, wherever anyone who lingers here too long ends up.

Story Master only: adventure seeds for this sphere.

A nervous scholar is convinced the Modrons will wake soon and needs proof: the heroes must take a Modron intact and pull the data from its clockwork body. An alchemist pays handsomely for raw Mechanus Oil, a poison potent enough to kill even the Exalted, especially in bulk; the trip in and out is risky, and storing the stuff aboard ship may be worse. Finally, someone must permanently shut down the Mechanus Portal Relay before the machines use it to escape, a hard task given it has run flawlessly for tens of millennia.
